notes.title: Punch people until their heads explode in Spartan Fist
notes.content:
There aren’t enough first-person games about simply punching people in the face, if you ask me (Zeno Clash is probably my favourite off the top of my head). Glass Bottom Games are trying to correct that with Spartan First [official site], a game that’s all about wait for it “punching dudes in the face so hard they explode”. Glorious.

It’s a first-person voxel-based brawler with plenty of cartoon blood. Judging by the trailer below you’ll be able to jab, hook, uppercut, and forward dash through a variety of enemies in a modern day Colosseum.

notes.title: Have You Played Hot Tin Roof: The Cat That Wore A Fedora?
notes.content:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day of the year, perhaps for all time.

How many games have made you laugh? Not a grin but a laugh. It doesn’t have to be an uncontrollable bark – a gentle chuckle is fine – but I bet you can’t think of all that many. Hot Tin Roof [official site] delighted me and made me laugh so many times.

notes.title: v1.3 adds improved lighting / performance
notes.content:
With v1.3, Hot Tin Roof now has some very nice baked lighting. This both makes things look a fair bit sexier and noir'ier on high end, AND makes the game a lot, lot better looking on low-end. It also also improves performance across the board, especially on high-end.

There's also some... new hidden stuff to find. That we're not going to talk about yet. Even if you find it. But have fun! :D

If you check out [url=https://www.humblebundle.com/weekly]this week's Humble Weekly Bundle[/url], you'll see you can get Hot Tin Roof: The Cat That Wore A Fedora for a tenner. We even throw in the OST!

If we happen to get picked by Valve for a Summer Sale Promo, we'll be $10 here as well, but that isn't super likely. They tend to feature deeper discounted older games. So I wouldn't hold your breath on the game getting any cheaper during this sale. ;)

notes.title: Hot Tin Roof v1.25 adds kickbutt gamepad support!
notes.content:
Along with a host of other small changes, v1.25 totally ditches the old janky gamepad support, and adds super fancy gamepad support. Which is to say it "just works," is fully rebindable, and you can even change the button graphics between Sony and MS standards to fit whatever you've got plugged into your PC. Neat!

We're also 10% off through May 3rd, to celebrate what constitutes the last major "polish" change we really wanted to get in there. Yay!

notes.title: v1.2 is free content - "Jooseppi Wants You!"
notes.content:
Along with a handful of fixes that aren't worth enumerating (lots of subtle small things), v1.2 adds free content to the base game. It adds Jooseppi, the mayoral candidate who fights for worker's rights, in as a character you can actually interact with.

To find him, walk over to where Hi-Table Gum Factory is. Jooseppi's (ratty as heck) campaign offices are to the right of that. He needs your help.

It's just a goofy little side-quest, and involves (almost) no platforming, and you'll probably have it done in 20 minutes. It, amongst other things, hopefully removes the need to grind boxes for bits for the later upgrades in the game, and gives you some other ways of affording the early upgrades. It also loops in a few of the characters I felt didn't get to say much in the base game, and gives you more ability to help them achieve their goals.

notes.title: v1.13 is live!
notes.content:
This fixes... a lot of things, but mostly it adds a lot of subtle and not-so-subtle hints, re-directors and context-adders meant to help folks not get lost.

Switches now generally have signage of some kind if they're critical, for instance, and the doors or whatever they interact with are marked with similar signage. We added a bunch of additional "reveal" cameras that fire off to show you what switches do, and arranged those cameras so that you can always see some contextual clues to tell you what door just opened.

The single biggest change is in Hi-Table. It is now (almost) impossible to leave Hi-Table, after you pick up the <ammo type> at least, without going through the upper offices and meeting the <important person> that some folks missed. Even if you do manage to leave early, a few key conversations will stop assuming <someone is in jail>, which will hopefully reduce confusion.

Finally, we tried to make it more obvious what different ammo types could do. Clues now fire off when you pick up ammo, so that you can refer back to what an ammo type does later, and those clues even let you ask Franky about them again in case you button-mashed through her explanation. Some Franky dialogs are also now a little more overt, and we made the Franky hint in Ossified Egg when you go back the second time effectively impossible to miss.

Oh, and it's now (very) possible to beat the game without ever doing the final Clue sweep to <get that warrant and do the thing>. It was technically possible before, but not easy - now there's a much easier way, which Mazuma sells, assuming you've bought both wallet upgrades. You won't get a bad ending at all (there's 14 different end states, none are bad), and hopefully that'll help the folks that just don't want to do a big hunt at that point.

We'll be rolling from here onto our first little content update. It won't be anything huge, mind, but it should hit around March 16th and adds a fun bit of narrative to the world. It involves Jooseppi, and loops in a few of the other lesser-used characters as well.

Linux People With Achievement Problems: No, this probably won't fix that bug. That's going to require, most likely, updating Steamworks, which we'll do in the next patch.

notes.title: A Tennessee Waltz: Hot Tin Roof
notes.content:
Jazz! It’s JK Simmons’ weapon of choice and it helped him on the road to Oscar glory. Noir! It’s shadows, killer quips and Walter Neff’s final cigarette. Cats! Invented as part of an early marketing campaign for AOL, cats became the most popular of the internet’s many fictional characters. Hot Tin Roof: The Cat That Wore A Fedora [official site] neatly combines jazz, noir and cats, and after playing briefly over the weekend, I can confirm that the combination is rather satisfying. A tasty jazz-noir cat-tale.
